question: Which private-equity rivals are most active in our sectors?
html:
Most active PE rivals by sector

Residential HVAC and plumbing is where rivals are most active: national consolidators and four PA/NJ buyers compete directly with Punctual Pros. Commercial electrical, legal IT and lab distribution each face one or two named challengers, with open space still available (Private-equity landscape).

Rivals by portfolio company

BSP portfolio companyMost active rivalsIntensity
Punctual ProsApex/Alpine, Wrench/LGP, TurnPoint/OMERS, Redwood/Altas, Any Hour/Knox Lane, T3/Riverside. Local: Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally (Watchtower), Northwinds (TruArc)Highest
CETKohlberg (RESA Power, Loenbro, CLEAResult); Huron (Criticore, Albireo)Rising, mostly outside New England
FrontlineAlpine's Evergreen, EagleTree/Integreon, BVNo direct sponsor-backed copy yet
Thomas ScientificCalibre ScientificOne main bidder

Residential services detail

  • Apex completed 46 add-ons in 2023 and 60 in 2025 (Home-services company case studies). That pace sets add-on pricing.
  • Not every rival can pay up. TurnPoint and Any Hour have moved to part-PIK interest and are marked at 89–94. Horizon pays 3.75% PIK, is marked 92.5 and was lender-owned by 2026. Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026 (Competitor filings).
  • Sila and Haller are the healthier local rivals. Sila's revenue is est. $450–650M, low confidence, built mostly through acquisitions (Competitor filings).

Electrical and fund-level peers

  • Cascade Partners reports that PE has made most electrical-contractor deals since 2023. The two to watch near CET are Albireo's Upstate NY expansion and Kohlberg's energy-efficiency cluster (Private-equity landscape).
  • IES is a public strategic buyer, not PE. It earns 11.4% operating margins with no net debt and can pay strategic prices in New England (Competitor filings).
  • The closest firm-level peers are MidOcean, CIVC, Trilantic North America, Palladium, Vesterra/Comvest and Bertram. BSP's roughly $335M fund competes against flagships of $0.9–2.1B (Private-equity landscape).

Gaps

  • The context names no rivals for Bully Pulpit International or Fair Harbor. Answering that needs sponsor deal logs for public-affairs and DTC apparel deals.
  • Some rival fund sizes are unknown because the search quota ran out (Private-equity landscape).

Next actions

  1. For Punctual Pros, track Horizon and Heartland as possible sources of distressed assets ahead of Dec 15, 2026. Keep proprietary outreach focused on shops below $3M EBITDA rather than joining auctions.
  2. For CET, speed up New England add-ons before Albireo or Kohlberg move into the six-state footprint.
  3. For Frontline, build a target list of law-firm MSP and billing-services businesses before Evergreen builds a legal vertical.
  4. Commission a rival scan for Bully Pulpit International and Fair Harbor to close the coverage gap.
